list: The official 55 trophies, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles before this guide was written. Names, descriptions and grades are PlayStation's own words; every guide below is written for this entry, in our own words, from the official description.
sources_note: Sources named per trophy: Exophase for the official name, description and grade; PSNProfiles for PSN's tracked counts and targets. Where a place or step is not pinned down by the official description, the guide says so plainly instead of inventing it.

trophies.guide: Earn the other 54 trophies and this one pops automatically — there is no separate task behind it. Follow the roadmap in order (story, then collectibles, then activities, then the long grinds) so the last trophy you need is a grind you can finish deliberately, not a story moment you have already passed. The gold trophy 'A Long Road' (100% completion) is the real final hurdle on the way here.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Play the opening mission Gone Fishing and follow its on-screen objectives to the end; it is the first story mission, so it cannot be missed. Treat it as a warm-up: learn the movement, driving and combat basics here, because every later mission builds on them. The trophy unlocks the moment the mission's closing scene finishes.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 in story order; the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Chapters are unmissable — just keep playing the main story and do not worry about skipping ahead. Use Chapter 1 to try the side activities that open up, since they feed the later activity trophies.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2; the trophy unlocks when the chapter ends. Keep an eye out for stranger missions and collectibles as new areas open, because several of them are easier to start the first time you pass through. Nothing in a chapter trophy can be missed — it is pure story progress.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3; the trophy pops at the chapter's close. By this point the map is wide open, so between story missions clear the collectibles and activities in each new district before moving on — backtracking later costs far more time. The chapter itself is unmissable.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4; the trophy unlocks when the chapter ends. Before the finale, check the missables page of this guide: the story-choice trophies and the one-time challenges are the only things a playthrough can actually lose, and Chapter 4 is your last comfortable chance to sweep them up. The chapter trophy itself cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete the game's final mission to earn this gold trophy. Make a manual save before starting it: the finale is the natural point to pause and finish any story-adjacent trophies you still need, and a save lets you replay the ending without replaying the chapter. The exact mission name and any choice inside it are not yet confirmed in-game, so this guide does not invent them.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run when it appears in your mission list. Story missions unlock in order, so if it is not offered yet, keep playing the main story. The trophy pops at the mission's end with no extra requirement.
trophies.name: Trust
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions usually ask for preparation first — stock up on ammo, armour and a fast getaway vehicle before you trigger it, and follow the crew's plan rather than improvising. The trophy unlocks when the heist concludes.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play when it unlocks in the main story. There is no side requirement: finish the mission and the trophy is yours. If the mission is not yet available, continue the story until the game offers it.
trophies.name: Family Matters
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners. The name suggests a high-profile set piece, so go in prepared — full health and armour, and a vehicle you can rely on for the escape. The trophy pops when the mission ends.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown, set at the Vice City International Airport. Expect heavy resistance around the airport, so clear a route out before the action starts and keep a fast vehicle nearby. The trophy unlocks at the mission's conclusion.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory. The name suggests a large-scale operation, so treat it like a heist: prepare first, then commit. The trophy pops when the operation is over — no extra objective is needed beyond finishing the mission.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion on the in-game stats screen: every story mission, stranger strand, collectible set, activity and challenge the game counts. This is the longest single requirement in the list and the true gate to the platinum, so track it from the start and clean up by category — story, then collectibles, then activities. The exact checklist the game counts toward 100% is not yet confirmed in-game, so check the stats screen in your own game rather than trusting any outside list.
trophies.name: A Long Road
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts — jumps, airtime, near-misses and trick driving — anywhere in Leonida. This is a pure volume grind: use fast bikes and cars, chain stunt jumps you already know, and let the count build passively while you travel between other objectives. The count is tracked by PSN, so watch it climb on your profile as you play.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list, tracked count: 250)

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type the game offers at least once — fishing, racing, the shooting range, arcade games, bowling, meditation and the rest. You only need to try each one, not master it, so this is a quick early trophy: work through the activities as they unlock and tick them off. The full list of activity types is not yet confirmed in-game, so use this guide's activity filter to see which ones you have tried.
trophies.name: Master of None
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — PSN tracks 42 of them. Learn each range's target pattern first with a bronze or silver run, then go for gold once you know the timing; steady aim beats fast trigger pulls. Ranges are repeatable, so a missed gold costs nothing but another attempt.
trophies.name: The Shootist
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN tracked count: 42 Shooting Range challenges)

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of its locations across Leonida. Drone racing rewards smooth lines over raw speed — cut corners gently and keep the drone level through gates instead of overcorrecting. The exact number of race locations is not yet confirmed in-game, so visit every Top Fun marker you find and win at each.
trophies.name: Top Fun
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — each race counts once, so variety matters more than repetition. Work through the race types (street, off-road, drone and any others the game offers) and pick a vehicle suited to each course. Races are repeatable, so a loss is just a retry.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Challenge Cal to a fishing contest and beat him. Fishing challenges reward patience and timing — watch the line tension, reel steadily, and do not rush the catch. This is flagged missable in this guide because a one-off rival challenge may not be repeatable: take it the first time Cal offers it, and keep a save from before the challenge just in case.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Play any arcade game through to its end. Arcades are found around Leonida — pick the game you find easiest and finish one full run. It only takes one completed game, so this is a quick trophy to grab early.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Work through Andy's stranger-mission strand until its final mission, then complete it. Stranger strands unlock as you explore, so check the map for Andy's marker whenever you are in a new district. The final mission is the payoff — finish it and the trophy pops.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Work through Kenton's stranger-mission strand until its final mission, then complete it. Keep Kenton's marker in mind as you travel — stranger missions often chain, and finishing one unlocks the next. The trophy unlocks at the end of the strand's last mission.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Work through Billy's stranger-mission strand until its final mission, then complete it. Stranger strands are easy to leave half-finished, so clear each one when you find it rather than saving them all for the endgame. The trophy pops when Billy's last mission ends.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full stranger-mission strands across Leonida. This is the umbrella trophy for the stranger system: each named stranger (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and others) has a strand, and finishing one counts toward the eight. Explore widely, answer every stranger marker, and finish strands as you find them.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Work through Randy's stranger-mission strand until its final mission, then complete it. Randy's strand counts toward the eight needed for 'Strangers & Freaks', so finishing it serves two trophies at once. The trophy unlocks at the end of the strand's last mission.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Work through Tyrone's stranger-mission strand until its final mission, then complete it. Like the other stranger strands, it is found by exploring and following map markers — check back in districts you have already visited, since new strands can appear as the story advances. The trophy pops when the final mission ends.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Find every meditation spot in Leonida and meditate at each one. Meditation spots are quiet scenic locations — check hilltops, beaches and viewpoints as you explore, and meditate at each spot you pass so you do not have to backtrack. The exact number of spots is not yet confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Unique hunts usually mean one specific animal in one specific place — track it carefully, take the shot cleanly, and bring the result back to Bret. This is flagged missable because a unique animal may only appear once: save before the hunt and do not scare it off carelessly. The animal and its location are not yet confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: Fair Game
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete three full collectible card sets by finding cards scattered across Leonida. Cards are a pure collectible grind — check shops, interiors and hidden corners as you explore, and trade duplicates if the game allows it. Finishing three sets (not just three cards) is the requirement, so keep collecting past the first set.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK feature at 100 different locations across Leonida. This is a volume collectible: make it a habit to WAiNK at every new place you visit — landmarks, businesses, viewpoints — and the count builds up naturally over a playthrough. The exact list of valid locations is not yet confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges of any kind. Challenges cover driving, combat, exploration and more — the game tracks them as you play, so just play broadly and check the challenges menu often to see which ones are close. Pick off the easy ones first and let the harder ones come with practice.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build up a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. Use the countryside or water to break line of sight, switch vehicles, and keep moving until the stars clear. This is flagged missable because it needs your partner present — do it while partner missions are available rather than after the story ends. Partner availability after the finale is not yet confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: Hot Together
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob three shops in a row without ever losing your wanted level — the trick is that you must stay wanted the whole time. Plan a route through three nearby shops, hit them fast, and keep the police chasing but not catching you between stops. Do it while your partner is available in the story; after the finale that may no longer be possible, which is why this guide flags it missable.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles across Leonida. Every new car, bike, boat or aircraft you get into counts — drive everything you see, check parking lots and docks, and vary your rides instead of sticking to one favourite. The count is tracked by PSN, so it climbs steadily as you explore.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Activate Combat Focus and take down five enemies before it ends. Pick a fight with a group — a gang hangout or a police chase with several officers close together — and trigger Combat Focus when they are clustered. Aim for quick, clean kills and do not waste the window on cover or reloading.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from Vice City International Airport — get a plane airborne without going through the normal departure process. Steal a plane on the tarmac and take off before airport security stops you. This is flagged missable only in the sense that it needs the airport open to you; the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in-game, so try the direct approach first.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: The description points at the Rhino tank, but the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in-game — this guide will not invent it. The sensible reading is to get into a Rhino and use it in combat, so keep an eye out for one at military areas or in missions that feature armour, and try driving and firing it there. If that does not pop it, the trigger is likely a specific Rhino moment in the story.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected at all — stealth is the whole requirement. Case the store first, go in quiet, avoid cameras and guards, and leave before anyone raises the alarm. This is flagged missable only because a blown attempt may lock the store down for a while; save beforehand and retry if you are spotted. The exact store or stores that count are not yet confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: Sneakthief
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape after each one. Plan each robbery like a small heist: know the vault's location, bring a fast escape vehicle, and break away from the police before the wanted level climbs out of control. Vaults are repeatable targets, so work through them one at a time.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Find an armored truck on the road, rob it, and escape the police response. Armored trucks travel set routes — intercept one in a quiet area, stop it, take the cash, and break line of sight before the wanted level builds. One clean robbery and escape is all it takes.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Visit every region of Leonida — Vice City, the beaches, the swamps, the countryside and every town in between. Exploration counts by area, so drive the full map methodically rather than fast-travelling everywhere; the in-game map shows which areas you have covered. Combine this with the collectible hunts so each trip earns double progress.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang in Leonida. Each gang runs its own operations, so you will need to find and hit one per gang — learn which gang controls which turf and look for their operations there. The number of gangs and the exact operations are not yet confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: Pest Control
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, find a bar or spot with a view, and enjoy a cocktail there. This is a pure flavour trophy — a quiet moment, not a challenge. Head to the beachfront at sunset, order a drink, and let the trophy pop.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle straight through a showroom's front window — the classic GTA exit. Pick a showroom, build up speed outside, and smash out through the glass. This is flagged missable only because a showroom may react differently after the fact; try it the first time you visit a showroom, and the exact showroom that counts is not yet confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: Capital Offense
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and bowl a proper follow-through — play a full game and finish your throws cleanly. Bowling is a repeatable activity, so there is no pressure: visit the alley, play through, and the trophy pops. It is flagged missable only if the alley is tied to a one-time story visit, so bowl the first time you are there to be safe.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — a partnership that appeals to the masses. The honest reading is that this comes from a story or side moment involving a public partnership, but the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in-game, so this guide does not invent one. Keep playing the story and side content; a trophy this vague usually pops from a scene you cannot miss.
trophies.name: Personal Best
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Make a story choice — the description is the game's own hint that a decision matters. This is the clearest missable trophy in the list: a choice, once made, may not be undoable in that playthrough. Save before any big story decision, and if the trophy does not pop, reload and choose differently. Which decision triggers it is not yet confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: The name says it: succeed on a second attempt at something you failed the first time. The likely reading is retrying a failed mission or challenge and passing it, but the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in-game. Play naturally — if you fail something, retry it rather than reloading an old save, and the trophy should come to you. Flagged missable because a perfect first-time playthrough might never trigger it.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Something strange happens — and the game knows it. This reads as a trophy for a rare or scripted odd event in the world, but the exact trigger is not yet confirmed in-game, so this guide does not invent one. Keep exploring odd corners of Leonida and playing the story; event trophies like this usually find you.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Perform a melee drive-by — attack with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle — and knock your targets over. A slow drive past a group on foot, weapon swinging, is the way to try it; a bike or an open vehicle gives the best reach. The exact targets that count are not yet confirmed in-game, so practise on groups of pedestrians away from heavy police patrols.
trophies.name: Ten Pin
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies and heists, and laundering turns them into clean cash — feed them through your contacts steadily rather than hoarding them. This is a long money grind, so pair it with the robbery trophies and the spending trophy.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops in Leonida — weapons, clothes, vehicles, food and everything else counts. Do not force it early: buy gear you actually need as you play, and the total climbs on its own. Late in the game, top it up with a big purchase such as a vehicle or property-adjacent spending.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property available in Leonida. Garages are bought with in-game money, so save up and purchase them as they appear on the market — they also give you somewhere to store the vehicles you need for the discovery trophy. The full list of garage properties is not yet confirmed in-game.
trophies.name: Little Boxes
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Use the app to register vehicles you find or own — any ten will do, so register each new ride as you get it instead of saving them all for the end. The app's exact menu is not yet confirmed in-game, but the requirement itself is simple: ten registrations.
trophies.name: On the Spot
sources: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list (official name, description and grade)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PSN trophy list)
